title: Climate Informed Dengue Prediction and Future Risk Under a Changing Monsoon Climate in Kerala, India.
design: machine-learning prediction (XGBoost and others) plus El Nino/La Nina composites and CMIP6 projections
enso_metric: Nino 3.4 SST anomaly (HadISST); El Nino/La Nina years by Nino 3.4
effect: El Nino-like conditions associated with higher dengue via warmer, drier pre-monsoon; La Nina opposite; best model R2 0.72 with all climate predictors (no ENSO-only estimate)
risk_of_bias: 14 years (few ENSO events); ML variable importance, not an effect estimate; local weather in the same models; trend handling unclear

title: Climatic drivers of the 2024 malaria outbreak in two neighbouring districts in northeastern India and its corridor: The indirect role of El Niño.
design: Poisson regression with lagged weather, ENSO main effects and ENSO x weather interactions; Granger tests
lags: ENSO 0-12 months (association at about 8-12 months); weather 0-6 months
effect: ENSO main effect significant in Alipurduar (2024 outbreak about 12 months after peak anomaly), not in Kokrajhar; ENSO modified weather-malaria associations
risk_of_bias: 7 years with one strong El Nino; many lagged terms (multiple testing); two districts; local weather adjusted

title: Strain variation and anomalous climate synergistically influence cholera pandemics.
setting: Bengal, Bombay Presidency, Punjab and Calcutta (former British India)
design: historical series with nonlinear time-series and scale-dependent correlation; event comparison around the 1904-07 El Nino
enso_metric: BEST ENSO index (historical, 1880-1939) with Kaplan SST; Nino 3.4 (late-20th-century comparison); El Nino/La Nina event years
lags: synchronisation within a few years of the 1904-07 El Nino
effect: cholera outbreaks synchronised over Bengal during the 1904-07 El Nino, with expansion after the Bombay invasion; no regression estimate for India
risk_of_bias: historical provinces include present Bangladesh and Pakistan; one dominant event; strain replacement confounds; scale-dependent correlations formally tested for Bangladesh strains

title: The changing relationship between Cholera and interannual climate variables in Kolkata over the past century.
effect: significant non-stationary coherence with ENSO in the historical interval; much weaker in 1999-2019
risk_of_bias: changes in surveillance and WASH between periods; non-stationarity; mediation by temperature suggested, not estimated

title: Weather integrated multiple machine learning models for prediction of dengue prevalence in India.
design: VAR, gradient boosting, SVR and LSTM prediction models
effect: cross-correlation with Nino3.4 r = 0.396 at lag 2 (p < 0.0001); Nino3.4 fourth of five predictors by relative importance; LSTM best (R2 0.86)
risk_of_bias: predictive models, no adjusted ENSO effect; 15 years; trend not removed for correlations

title: El Niño Southern Oscillation as an early warning tool for dengue outbreak in India.
setting: all states (state-level correlations); Delhi and Visakhapatnam monthly
design: Pearson correlation of case index with seasonal positive ONI; ENSO-phase maps
enso_metric: ONI (seasonal positive values; El Nino/La Nina/neutral phases)
effect: positive correlation in some states (e.g. Arunachal Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Uttarakhand, Delhi), negative in others (e.g. Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha)
risk_of_bias: unadjusted correlations; no trend or reporting-change control; many state tests; about 20 points per state

title: Lag effect of climatic variables on dengue burden in India.
design: Pearson cross-correlation of dengue with Nino3.4 and DMI (ENSO not in a regression model); distributed lag non-linear models for weather only
effect: synchronous r = 0.3 with Nino3.4; positive correlation at 3-6 month lags; r = 0.5 in 2015, -0.6 in 2016
risk_of_bias: 8 years; unadjusted correlations for ENSO; IDSP reporting changes

title: El Niño Southern Oscillation as an early warning tool for malaria outbreaks in India.
design: Pearson correlation of malaria case index with positive winter ONI; GIS maps
effect: state correlations from -0.5 to +0.7 (p < 0.05 where significant); positive in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar, Goa and others
risk_of_bias: unadjusted correlations; 22 annual points; programme and reporting changes; many state tests
